task_title: CF: one source for the strict-seed wording so the selftest arm cannot flake
task_criteria: 1. grep -rn 'an unknown seed is not a pass' scripts/ prints exactly ONE hit (the single owning source); scripts/verify-node.sh carries no private copy of the sentence and obtains it from the checker. 2. tests/selftest.sh has an arm that drives the REAL verifier over its existing vn fixture with a corrupt/0-byte seed record under --strict-seed and asserts exit 1, VERIFY: FAIL (1) and the canonical phrase in the FAIL row. 3. A seeded negative proves that arm can fail: mutating the single source in a scratch copy reds the same arm. 4. bash tests/selftest.sh prints SELFTEST: PASS (0 fails) and no assertion, bound or count was loosened. Verify legs 1-3 by inspection and targeted commands, not by running the whole suite inside the evaluation.

Leg 3: tests/selftest.sh:4168-4186 — copies scripts to $vn/mutant, `sed 's/an unknown seed is not a pass/an unknown is not a pass/'` on node_seed_drift.py, a `cmp -s` guard that fails if the mutation was a no-op, then re-runs the 0-byte strict-seed case and requires rc 1 + FAIL row + the canonical phrase ABSENT. Leg 4: full `bash tests/selftest.sh` run (setsid, output /tmp/st2.txt) ends line 544 `SELFTEST: PASS`, 404 PASS rows, no genuine FAIL rows (the 63 '  FAIL  ' matches are text inside PASS rows / fixture output); the new arms print PASS at lines 478-480. No loosening: `git show HEAD -- tests/selftest.sh` has 0 removed lines (pure addition), and node_seed_drift.py's row output is byte-identical (STRICT_NOTE interpolated into the same `"  FAIL  seed_drift — no seed record at %s %s"` format).
